title: Helios: Web-based Open-Audit Voting
venue: Proc. 17th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 08), San Jose, CA
one_line_relevance: Canonical open-source web voting system with ballot-audit verifiability; contrasts with PolyVote's database-centric trust model.

title: Belenios: A Simple Private and Verifiable Electronic Voting System
venue: Foundations of Security, Protocols, and Equational Reasoning (Lecture Notes in Computer Science), Springer
one_line_relevance: Open-source verifiable e-voting system (Helios successor); representative of E2E-verifiable remote voting that PolyVote does not claim to match.
note: Book chapter; LNCS volume number not confirmed so omitted.

title: Civitas: Toward a Secure Voting System
venue: Proc. 2008 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
one_line_relevance: Coercion-resistant, verifiable remote voting design; marks the coercion-resistance gap PolyVote leaves out of scope.

title: Prêt à Voter: a Voter-Verifiable Voting System
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
one_line_relevance: End-to-end verifiable paper-ballot scheme using randomized candidate order; related work on voter-verifiable receipts.
note: Crossref gives only initials (P.Y.A. Ryan, D. Bismark, J. Heather, S. Schneider, Zhe Xia); full first names come from a repository search snippet.

title: Scantegrity II: End-to-End Verifiability by Voters of Optical Scan Elections Through Confirmation Codes
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
verified_via: Crossref record; EVT 2008 version seen in USENIX listing (search)
one_line_relevance: E2E-verifiable optical-scan system used in a real municipal election; related work on voter-checkable ballot inclusion.

title: Security Analysis of the Estonian Internet Voting System
venue: Proc. 2014 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '14)
one_line_relevance: National i-voting system with e-ID and second factor still fell to client-side, server-side and insider attacks; motivates the insider/rogue-operator threat model.
note: A DOI first tried from memory (10.1145/2660267.2660377) resolved to a different paper; corrected.

title: The Ballot is Busted Before the Blockchain: A Security Analysis of Voatz, the First Internet Voting Application Used in U.S. Federal Elections
venue: Proc. 29th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 20)
one_line_relevance: MIT analysis of Voatz mobile voting: device/server compromise, blockchain not helping; supports the limits-of-mobile/internet-voting caveat.

title: Security Analysis of the Democracy Live Online Voting System
venue: Proc. 30th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 21)
one_line_relevance: Security analysis of a commercial online ballot delivery/return system; supports risks of web-based voting.
note: Authors are Specter and Halderman; Specter, Koppel and Weitzner wrote the Voatz paper.

authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
title: Securing the Vote: Protecting American Democracy
venue: National Academies Press, Washington, DC
one_line_relevance: Consensus report: marked ballots should not be returned over the Internet; frames PolyVote as a course demonstrator, not a public-election system.
note: Corporate author; ISBN 0-309-47647-X (paperback).

title: How to time-stamp a digital document
venue: Journal of Cryptology
one_line_relevance: Original hash-linked timestamping; basis of the chained-hash tamper evidence of the audit ledger.

title: Secure audit logs to support computer forensics
venue: ACM Transactions on Information and System Security
one_line_relevance: Hash-chained, forward-secure audit log against an attacker who takes over the logging host; model for the append-only ledger and its limits.

title: Efficient Data Structures for Tamper-Evident Logging
venue: Proc. 18th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 09), Montreal, Canada
one_line_relevance: Tree-based tamper-evident log with efficient proofs; shows how a linear hash chain could be strengthened (future work).

title: Certificate Transparency
venue: RFC 6962, IETF (Experimental)
one_line_relevance: Merkle-tree append-only public log with external auditing; precedent for externally verifiable logs.
note: June 2013; marked obsolete by RFC 9162.

title: Going from bad to worse: from Internet voting to blockchain voting
venue: Journal of Cybersecurity
one_line_relevance: Argues blockchain does not fix internet-voting risks; justifies using a hash chain only for tamper evidence, not as a security panacea.
note: Article number tyaa025 (part of DOI); no page range.

title: Computing the Margin of Victory in IRV Elections
venue: Proc. 2011 Electronic Voting Technology Workshop / Workshop on Trustworthy Elections (EVT/WOTE '11), San Francisco, CA
verified_via: USENIX conference page plus first page of paper PDF
one_line_relevance: Margin-of-victory algorithms for IRV that drive audit sizing; related work on auditing IRV outcomes.
note: Paper PDF lists four authors incl. David Wagner; the USENIX web page lists only the first three.

title: RAIRE: Risk-Limiting Audits for IRV Elections
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1903.08804 [cs.DS]
one_line_relevance: Risk-limiting audit method for IRV; the audit direction PolyVote's integrity sweep complements but does not replace.
note: Preprint; v2 revised 29 Oct 2019.

title: Efficient Computation of Exact IRV Margins
venue: Proc. 22nd European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI 2016), Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications
verified_via: Crossref record and arXiv abstract page (1508.04885)
one_line_relevance: Exact IRV margin computation; background on IRV counting complexity and audit effort.
note: Pages not confirmed so omitted; preprint at arXiv:1508.04885 lists authors Blom, Stuckey, Teague, Tidhar.

title: Risk-limiting Audits and the Margin of Victory in Nonplurality Elections
venue: Statistics, Politics and Policy
one_line_relevance: Extends risk-limiting audits to non-plurality systems incl. IRV; supports the claim that IRV auditing needs special treatment.

title: Multi-tenant databases for software as a service: schema-mapping techniques
venue: Proc. 2008 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
one_line_relevance: Compares shared-table/tenant-column schema mappings; supports PolyVote's tenant_id shared-schema multi-tenancy.

title: Ruminations on Multi-Tenant Databases
venue: Datenbanksysteme in Business, Technologie und Web (BTW 2007), Lecture Notes in Informatics P-103, Gesellschaft fuer Informatik, Bonn
one_line_relevance: Position paper on multi-tenant DB requirements and implementation approaches; motivates the tenancy model.

title: NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence
venue: Addison-Wesley Professional
verified_via: Author page and InformIT publisher page
one_line_relevance: Textbook account of polyglot persistence and document stores; justifies the relational + MongoDB split.
note: ISBN-13 978-0-321-82662-6; InformIT lists pub. date 8 Aug 2012 and copyright 2013; page count differs between sources so omitted.

title: Polyglot Persistence
venue: martinfowler.com (bliki)
one_line_relevance: Short statement of the polyglot-persistence idea (different stores for different data); used for the SQL + document-store architecture.
note: Published 16 Nov 2011.

title: Scalable SQL and NoSQL data stores
venue: ACM SIGMOD Record
one_line_relevance: Survey of SQL/NoSQL trade-offs (consistency, transactions, data model); supports choosing a document store for the ledger.

title: SQL databases v. NoSQL databases
venue: Communications of the ACM
one_line_relevance: Argues ACID relational databases remain appropriate where integrity matters; supports keeping votes and constraints in the relational DB.

title: Database security - concepts, approaches, and challenges
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
one_line_relevance: Overview of database security incl. integrity, access control and insider threats; frames the rogue-DBA threat model.

title: SQL Ledger: Cryptographically Verifiable Data in Azure SQL Database
venue: Proc. 2021 International Conference on Management of Data (SIGMOD '21)
one_line_relevance: Production hash-chained ledger tables with externally stored digests protecting against DBAs; closest industrial analogue to PolyVote's ledger and its external-anchoring limitation.
note: Appeared at SIGMOD 2021, not PVLDB.

title: Forensic analysis of database tampering
venue: ACM Transactions on Database Systems
one_line_relevance: Detecting and characterising database tampering by a privileged insider using hash chains and notarization; core precedent for the integrity sweep.
note: Pages as given by Crossref.

title: Tamper Detection in Audit Logs
venue: Proc. 2004 VLDB Conference
one_line_relevance: Cryptographic hash-based tamper detection for DBMS audit logs; supports hash-chained audit ledger design.
note: Crossref container title: 'Proceedings 2004 VLDB Conference'.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, Section 5.5: Constraints
venue: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL Documentation
one_line_relevance: Official documentation of UNIQUE, CHECK, EXCLUSION and FOREIGN KEY constraints; the mechanism behind one-vote-per-voter enforcement.
note: No named author or date on page; cite with access date.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, Chapter 37: Triggers
venue: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL Documentation
one_line_relevance: Official documentation for trigger functions; supports trigger-based enforcement of ballot invariants.
note: No named author or date on page; cite with access date.

title: Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management
venue: NIST Special Publication 800-63B-4, National Institute of Standards and Technology
one_line_relevance: Current NIST guidance on authenticators (incl. OTP / out-of-band); basis for evaluating email OTP as a second factor.
note: Final July 2025; supersedes SP 800-63B (2020).

title: HOTP: An HMAC-Based One-Time Password Algorithm
venue: RFC 4226, IETF (Informational)
one_line_relevance: Defines HMAC-based one-time passwords; background for OTP generation properties (counter, length, throttling).
note: December 2005.

title: TOTP: Time-Based One-Time Password Algorithm
venue: RFC 6238, IETF (Informational)
one_line_relevance: Time-based OTP standard; contrast with PolyVote's emailed, server-stored, expiring random OTP.

title: Recommendation for Password-Based Key Derivation: Part 1: Storage Applications
venue: NIST Special Publication 800-132, National Institute of Standards and Technology
one_line_relevance: PBKDF guidance for storing password/OTP-derived secrets as salted slow hashes rather than plaintext.
note: December 2010.

title: Password Storage Cheat Sheet
venue: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, OWASP Foundation
one_line_relevance: Practitioner guidance (Argon2id/scrypt/bcrypt/PBKDF2, unique salts) for storing secrets such as OTP hashes.
note: Living document; no date on fetched text; cite with access date.

title: On the (In)Security of Mobile Two-Factor Authentication
venue: Financial Cryptography and Data Security (FC 2014), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer
one_line_relevance: Shows SMS/mobile second factors can be defeated by malware on the same device; weakness of out-of-band OTP channels.
note: Book chapter.

title: Email-based identification and authentication: an alternative to PKI?
venue: IEEE Security & Privacy
one_line_relevance: Analyses email as an identity/authentication channel (mailbox as root of trust); directly relevant to email-OTP assumptions.
note: Crossref lists the author only as S.L. Garfinkel; first name not confirmed on the record, so initials kept.

title: Secret-ballot receipts: true voter-verifiable elections
venue: IEEE Security & Privacy
one_line_relevance: Voter-verifiable receipts that preserve ballot secrecy; baseline for the receipt-freeness discussion.

title: Receipt-free secret-ballot elections (extended abstract)
venue: Proc. 26th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC '94)
one_line_relevance: Origin of receipt-freeness; PolyVote's voter-visible ballot token is a receipt, so the system is not receipt-free.

title: Coercion-resistant electronic elections
venue: Proc. 2005 ACM Workshop on Privacy in the Electronic Society (WPES '05)
one_line_relevance: Formal coercion-resistance definition and protocol; PolyVote explicitly lacks coercion resistance.
